princess-maritza: Percy James Brebner spins a romantic adventure in the popular Ruritanian style. Princess Maritza, caught between duty to her throne and the pull of love, navigates court plots and daring escapes in a storybook European kingdom. Light, gallant, and swiftly paced, it is exactly the sort of tale that delighted readers hungry for royalty and romance.
the-old-roman-world-the-grandeur-and-fai: John Lord's popular lectures trace Rome's rise and fall — the grandeur of its civilization and the causes of its failure. Written for general readers, the narrative moves from republic to empire with moral reflection. A Victorian classic of popular history, earnest and instructive.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acerenza: This 1913 reference article on Acerenza — the hilltop diocese of southern Italy. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its history. Its cathedral crowns a Lucanian crag. An ancient see in a rugged land. Its Norman castle guards the valley road. Bishops have sat there since the Lombards.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aenas-of-gaza: A 1913 entry on Aeneas of Gaza — the Christian philosopher of the dialogue Theophrastus. William Turner explains his Platonism. He argued the soul's immortality. Athens' wisdom met Gaza's faith. A late flower of Christian philosophy. His dialogue survives in a single manuscript.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-escob: This 1913 reference article on Escobar y Mendoza — the Jesuit prince of probabilism. James David O'Neill notes his many tomes. His moral theology filled the schools. Pascal mocked his laxity. A casuist of world-wide fame. His Liber theologiae filled the presses.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aymeric-of-pi: A 1913 entry on Aymeric of Piacenza — the Dominican Master General. Thomas Schwertner honors his learned rule. He led the order's golden age. The friars prized their chief. A general of the Preachers. His order honors its master. His generalate guided the Preachers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolome-car: A 1913 entry on Bartolomé Carranza — the Archbishop of Toledo. Johann Peter Kirsch tells his tragic trial. The Inquisition held him seventeen years. Rome at last absolved the prelate. The most famous trial of the Spanish Church. His Catechism served the Spanish church.
